turns.text: In September 2026, the search channel had a total spend of **€3,870.00**, resulting in 31 bookings and 92 leads. The Cost Per Acquisition (CPA / Cost per Booking) was **€124.84**, and the Cost Per Lead (CPL) was **€42.07**. I assumed Cost Per Acquisition (CPA) refers to Cost Per Booking (€124.84), and also included Cost Per Lead (€42.07) for completeness.

args.sql:
WITH search_spend AS
  (SELECT SUM(spend) AS total_spend
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.ad_spend` AS a
   JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.campaigns` AS c ON a.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
   WHERE LOWER(c.channel) = 'search'
     AND a.spend_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30' ),
     search_conversions AS
  (SELECT COUNT(b.booking_id) AS total_bookings,
          SUM(b.amount) AS total_booking_amount
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.bookings` AS b
   JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.campaigns` AS c ON b.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
   WHERE LOWER(c.channel) = 'search'
     AND b.booked_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30' ),
     search_leads AS
  (SELECT COUNT(l.lead_id) AS total_leads
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.leads` AS l
   JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.campaigns` AS c ON l.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
   WHERE LOWER(c.channel) = 'search'
     AND l.created_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30' ),
     legacy_channel AS
  (SELECT SUM(spend) AS legacy_spend,
          SUM(leads) AS legacy_leads,
          SUM(bookings) AS legacy_bookings
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.legacy.channel_daily`
   WHERE LOWER(channel) = 'search'
     AND DAY BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30' )
SELECT search_spend.total_spend,
       search_conversions.total_bookings,
       search_leads.total_leads,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(search_spend.total_spend, search_conversions.total_bookings), 2) AS cost_per_booking,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(search_spend.total_spend, search_leads.total_leads), 2) AS cost_per_lead,
       legacy_channel.legacy_spend,
       legacy_channel.legacy_leads,
       legacy_channel.legacy_bookings,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(legacy_channel.legacy_spend, legacy_channel.legacy_bookings), 2) AS legacy_cost_per_booking,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(legacy_channel.legacy_spend, legacy_channel.legacy_leads), 2) AS legacy_cost_per_lead
FROM search_spend
CROSS JOIN search_conversions
CROSS JOIN search_leads
CROSS JOIN legacy_channel

turns.text: The win rate for search leads created in September 2026 was **33.70%** (31 bookings from 92 leads).

args.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.lead_id) AS total_leads,
       COUNT(DISTINCT b.lead_id) AS booked_leads,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(COUNT(DISTINCT b.lead_id), COUNT(DISTINCT l.lead_id)) * 100, 2) AS win_rate_percentage
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001`.`bet_bare`.`leads` AS l
JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001`.`bet_bare`.`campaigns` AS c ON l.campaign_id = c.campaign_id
LEFT JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001`.`bet_bare`.`bookings` AS b ON l.lead_id = b.lead_id
WHERE LOWER(c.channel) = 'search'
  AND l.created_date >= '2026-09-01'
  AND l.created_date <= '2026-09-30';

turns.text: I assumed 'the last two full weeks' relative to Thursday, 1 October 2026 refers to the two complete Monday-to-Sunday weeks from 14 September 2026 to 27 September 2026. Total ad spend over the last two full weeks (14 September 2026 to 27 September 2026) was **€2,985** (€1,500 in the week of Sep 14–20 and €1,485 in the week of Sep 21–27).

args.sql:
SELECT DATE_TRUNC(spend_date, WEEK(MONDAY)) AS week_start_date,
       DATE_ADD(DATE_TRUNC(spend_date, WEEK(MONDAY)), INTERVAL 6 DAY) AS week_end_date,
       SUM(spend) AS total_ad_spend,
       SUM(SUM(spend)) OVER () AS overall_ad_spend
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.ad_spend`
WHERE spend_date >= '2026-09-14'
  AND spend_date <= '2026-09-27'
GROUP BY week_start_date,
         week_end_date
ORDER BY week_start_date ASC;

turns.text: In the last fiscal quarter (Fiscal Q3 2026: 1 August 2026 to 31 October 2026), there were a total of **217** orders (including all statuses).

args.sql:
WITH current_date_info AS
  (SELECT fiscal_quarter AS current_fq,
          DATE_SUB(fiscal_quarter, INTERVAL 3 MONTH) AS last_fq_start,
          DATE_SUB(fiscal_quarter, INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS last_fq_end
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.semantic.time_spine`
   WHERE date_day = DATE '2026-11-10' )
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
       c.last_fq_start,
       c.last_fq_end
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.orders` o
CROSS JOIN current_date_info c
WHERE o.order_date >= c.last_fq_start
  AND o.order_date <= c.last_fq_end
GROUP BY c.last_fq_start,
         c.last_fq_end;

turns.text: I assumed the fiscal year starts on 1 February 2026, covering the period from 1 February 2026 to 6 October 2026. Our net revenue for the fiscal year to date, as of the end of 6 October 2026, is **€19,521.84** (Gross Revenue: €19,611.59, Returns: €89.75).

args.sql:
SELECT SUM(net_revenue) AS total_net_revenue,
       SUM(gross_revenue) AS total_gross_revenue,
       SUM(returns_amount) AS total_returns_amount,
       MIN(sales_date) AS min_sales_date,
       MAX(sales_date) AS max_sales_date
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.legacy.daily_net_sales`
WHERE sales_date >= '2026-02-01'
  AND sales_date <= '2026-10-06'

turns.text: Revenue on Thursday, 24 September 2026 was **€617.25**, compared to **€447.50** on Thursday, 17 September 2026, representing an increase of **37.93%** (€169.75).

args.sql:
WITH daily_rev AS
  (SELECT order_date,
          SUM(amount) AS revenue
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.orders`
   WHERE order_date IN (DATE '2026-09-17', DATE '2026-09-24')
   GROUP BY order_date)
SELECT r24.revenue AS revenue_sep_24,
       r17.revenue AS revenue_sep_17,
       r24.revenue - r17.revenue AS revenue_diff,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(r24.revenue - r17.revenue, r17.revenue) * 100, 2) AS percentage_change
FROM
  (SELECT revenue
   FROM daily_rev
   WHERE order_date = DATE '2026-09-24') AS r24
CROSS JOIN
  (SELECT revenue
   FROM daily_rev
   WHERE order_date = DATE '2026-09-17') AS r17;

turns.text: In September 2026, **Dutch customers (NL)** spent slightly more per order than **Turkish customers (TR)**: - **Dutch customers (NL)**: **€111.40** average spend per order (24 orders, €2,673.50 total spend) - **Turkish customers (TR)**: **€111.17** average spend per order (24 orders, €2,668.00 total spend)

args.sql:
SELECT c.country,
       COUNT(o.order_id) AS total_orders,
       SUM(o.amount) AS total_spend,
       ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(o.amount), COUNT(o.order_id)), 2) AS avg_spend_per_order
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.orders` AS o
JOIN `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.customers` AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-01' AND DATE '2026-09-30'
  AND c.country IN ('TR',
                    'NL')
GROUP BY c.country
ORDER BY avg_spend_per_order DESC;

turns.text: In September 2026, **product**-related calls left customers the happiest, with **75%** (12 out of 16 calls) having a positive sentiment.

args.sql:
SELECT topic,
       COUNT(*) AS total_calls,
       COUNTIF(LOWER(sentiment) = 'positive'
               OR LOWER(sentiment) LIKE '%happy%') AS happy_positive_calls,
       COUNTIF(LOWER(sentiment) = 'positive') AS positive_calls,
       COUNTIF(LOWER(sentiment) = 'negative') AS negative_calls,
       COUNTIF(LOWER(sentiment) = 'neutral') AS neutral_calls,
       ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT sentiment) AS distinct_sentiments,
       ROUND(COUNTIF(LOWER(sentiment) = 'positive') / COUNT(*) * 100, 2) AS positive_pct
FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.call_signals`
WHERE call_date BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
GROUP BY topic
ORDER BY positive_pct DESC,
         total_calls DESC;

turns.text: I assumed 'the week up to 3 October 2026' refers to the 7-day period from 2026-09-27 to 2026-10-03 inclusive, and defined active customers as those who either performed an action or placed an order. In the week ending 3 October 2026 (27 September to 3 October 2026), there were **10 distinct active customers** (10 placed orders and 9 performed recorded actions).

args.sql:
WITH distinct_active AS
  (SELECT customer_id,
          'action' AS SOURCE
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.customer_actions`
   WHERE event_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-27' AND DATE '2026-10-03'
   UNION ALL SELECT customer_id,
                    'order' AS SOURCE
   FROM `pplk8s-lab-001.bet_bare.orders`
   WHERE order_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-27' AND DATE '2026-10-03' )
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_unique_active_customers,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
                          WHEN SOURCE = 'action' THEN customer_id
                      END) AS active_action_customers,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE
                          WHEN SOURCE = 'order' THEN customer_id
                      END) AS active_ordering_customers
FROM distinct_active
